items.name: disclosure_form (CX-10..CX-18)
items.current_text:
Question to jev: *What kind of document is this page?* One value. If several fit, take the first in table order.

- `register_cross_institution`: The page is, or is one entry in, a structured list of AI or algorithmic systems kept by a government body, with several entries in a common format (inventory, register, catalogue, algorithmic transparency record in a standard template), **and the list covers more than one institution** (a national or sectoral register, a standard-template record series across agencies).
- `register_single_institution`: As CX-10, but the list covers **one institution only** (e.g. a city's own table of its AI tools).
- `mandated_report`: The page is a document produced to meet a reporting obligation, such as a statutory annual-report section or a compliance or transparency report under a named rule.
- CX-13: The obligation may be named on the page **or inferred from the document's genre** (e.g. an annual report, a statutory compliance report). This is the one stated exception to CX-03.
- `formal_record`: An official one-off document of record from a government body: adopted policy or guidance, legislation, council or board minutes or resolutions, budget documents, procurement notice or award, audit or inspection report, **response to a freedom-of-information request**.
- `informal_official`: A government body's own communication with no reporting obligation and no standard format: press release, news item, blog, social post, speech, event page, service or FAQ page.
- `third_party`: Not published by a government body: news, vendor, academic, NGO or policy organization. A register entry quoted in a news article is `third_party` (code the page, not what it quotes).
- `unknown`: The page's kind cannot be determined from its text (e.g. an archived fragment with no header).

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:35-36 (CX-12, CX-13); pilot/pilot.py:132 (question text: 'The obligation may be named on the page or inferred from the document's genre (e.g. an annual report)')
findings.text: `mandated_report` is the top of the 'systematic' pole, but CX-12/13 do not require the obligation to concern AI or algorithmic disclosure. Any statutory annual report (most ministries, councils and agencies publish one by law) that mentions a chatbot in passing would code `mandated_report`, placing an incidental mention above a city's own AI register. CX-13 lets jev infer the obligation from genre, which is world knowledge (an exception to CX-03) and varies by country. Pilot counts are too small to test this: 3 of 285 (PILOT-REPORT.md:21) and 2 in pilot 2 (report-v2.json distribution).

The 'first in table order' tie-break puts the register values first, while CX-16 says a register entry quoted in a news article is `third_party`. A trade-press page reproducing a register entry fits both CX-10 (it 'is one entry in' a list) and CX-16, and the order rule points to the register. The question text (pilot.py:197) adds 'not what it quotes', which mitigates this but sits outside the frozen CX rows.

No value fits several common page kinds cleanly: a government-hosted PDF of a vendor or consultant report; a page of a state-owned enterprise or public university (institutions the master includes); a joint statement by a government body and a vendor; an official Wayback copy (extract contract §4.6 `archive`, output_contract.md:216). Each forces a choice between `formal_record`, `informal_official`, `third_party` and `unknown` without a rule.

findings.evidence: SPEC.md:97-98 (R-040, R-041); INDEX-DECISIONS.md:33 (P-5 new fields = b: unknown form excluded from the denominator)
findings.text: Genre is a whole-document judgement with no natural verbatim anchor. Under R-040/R-041 every non-`unknown` value needs a quote. If the extractor cannot find a quote that 'supports' `informal_official`, the code is downgraded to `unknown`, and P-5 (b) then drops the page from the transparency denominator. Downgrades would fall unevenly by page kind (a press release header is quotable; a policy PDF's genre often is not), which biases the index composition.

findings.evidence: PILOT-REPORT.md:33, :61; Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: disclosure_form 39/285
findings.text: Agent read 39/1/0 on 40 pages in both pilots, but the 40 pages are one model's read of 6,000-character excerpts and only 4 were rare-form pages (PILOT-REPORT.md:15); register values had 1 case. 39 of 285 pilot-2 answers were below the 0.8 threshold and would be downgraded under R-081 (SPEC.md:133).

`third_party` duplicates the publisher dimension of `source_type` (§4.6). In v2.7 `source_type` has no coder (see X21), so the QC cross-check in CX §2 has nothing to check against unless X21 is resolved.

options.label: Keep CX-10..CX-18 as signed
options.mechanism: One jev Choice in pass 1, first chunk's value (R-044), with the pilot-2 question text.
options.benefits: No re-signature; the most reliable CX field on the pilot read; matches the signed index design.
options.risks: `mandated_report` over-captures statutory annual reports; genre codes may be downgraded for lack of a quote; boundary pages unresolved.
options.commits_to: R-025 byte-identical text; needs the X14 downgrade rule to say which supporting text counts for a genre code.

options.label: Agent-drafted: require an AI-related obligation for mandated_report
options.mechanism: Re-word CX-12/13: `mandated_report` only when the obligation concerns reporting on AI, algorithms or digital systems, named on the page; genre inference allowed only for documents whose title names AI/algorithmic reporting. Otherwise statutory annual reports code `formal_record`.
options.benefits: Restores the 'systematic AI disclosure' construct; removes a CX-03 exception; gives the extractor a quotable anchor (the named rule).
options.risks: Lower `mandated_report` counts (already ~1%); re-opens D-B (b), a signed PI ruling.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-12/13 (D-B); fixture pages for the new boundary (R-084); no enum change, so no version steps beyond the v2.7 already planned.

options.label: Agent-drafted: split publisher from genre
options.mechanism: Two jev Choices: `publisher_kind` (this institution / other government body / non-government / unknown) and `document_genre` (register entry / mandated report / formal record / informal communication / unknown). `disclosure_form` becomes a deterministic cross of the two; `third_party` = publisher non-government.
options.benefits: Each question is simpler; removes the order tie-break; `publisher_kind` can replace the publisher half of `source_type` (X21) and supports the `other_body` boundary.
options.risks: Two questions where one was piloted; the derived value may differ from the signed one on edge cases; new enums.
options.commits_to: Re-signature and a re-pilot of both questions; enum additions (two version steps, C-007); index decision 7 re-read against the new values.

options.label: Agent-drafted: quote rule for genre codes
options.mechanism: Keep the wording; state in the X14 downgrade rule that genre codes are supported by the page's title or heading line (deterministic `source_title` plus the first heading), not by an extractor quote, and are exempt from R-041 downgrade if a title exists.
options.benefits: Avoids systematic `unknown` from missing quotes; no change to frozen wording.
options.risks: A title is weak evidence for genre; exempts one field class from G-002 'verbatim support'.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-041 (PI approval, not CX re-signature); fixture check in T-024.

items.notes: **Frozen (CX-01.2, signed 2026-10-25; SPEC R-025, SPEC.md:78).** Any alternative below other than `keep` requires PI re-signature of the CX row, a re-pilot or at least the R-084 fixture test for the changed wording, and (for any enum change) two contract-version steps (C-007, SPEC.md:221). T-011 must stay byte-identical to the signed text unless re-signed (PLAN.md T-011).

items.name: disclosure_scope (CX-20..CX-25)
items.current_text:
- `whole_of_government`: The listing or document the page belongs to covers institutions across the government (all central agencies, or all units of a level).
- `multi_institution`: It covers several institutions, but not government-wide (a sector, a region, a group of agencies).
- `single_institution`: It covers one institution only.
- `unknown`: Coverage cannot be determined from the page.
- CX-25: which pages are coded: All pages.

findings.evidence: Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: disclosure_scope 136/285 (48%); report-v2.json confidence_quartiles disclosure_scope [p10 0.37, p25 0.59, p50 0.81, p75 0.95]
findings.text: Nearly half of pilot-2 scope answers fall below 0.8. Under R-081 (SPEC.md:133) each goes to `unknown`, which for a 4-value field is an existing value, so the field silently becomes about half `unknown`. Low confidence is spread across values (78 single, 53 multi, 5 whole-of-government).

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:52-54; pilot/pilot.py:198-199 ('How many institutions does the listing or document this page belongs to cover?')
findings.text: For non-register pages (about 98% of the pilot, PILOT-REPORT.md:21), 'the document covers' reads as 'how many institutions the activity involves', not 'how wide the disclosure system is'. A ministry press release announcing a government-wide Copilot rollout codes `whole_of_government`, which is the PI's 'whole-of-government' pole, although the disclosure itself is an ad-hoc press release. The field then overlaps `activity_type = program_initiative` rather than measuring the disclosure channel. Kaser's `branch_coverage` is coded per disclosure system, not per page (codebook-extension-proposal.md:58).

`single_institution` is substantive under R-041 but is usually an absence (the page mentions no other body). There is rarely a verbatim quote for 'covers one institution only', so it will be downgraded to `unknown` unless treated as a no-evidence value.
Scope is taken from the first chunk. For a long register or inventory PDF, the institution list often starts after the introduction, so the first chunk may not show coverage.

options.label: Keep CX-20..CX-25 as signed
options.mechanism: One jev Choice in pass 1 on all pages; first chunk.
options.benefits: No re-signature; matches D-C (a) and D-D (b).
options.risks: About half `unknown` after R-081 on pilot evidence; construct drift on non-register pages.
options.commits_to: R-025; the X15 threshold rule decides how many become `unknown`.

options.label: Agent-drafted: code scope only on register and mandated pages
options.mechanism: Ask `disclosure_scope` only when `disclosure_form` in {register_cross_institution, register_single_institution, mandated_report}; otherwise store `_NA_`.
options.benefits: Scope then measures the disclosure system as intended; fewer low-confidence answers; cheaper.
options.risks: Reverses D-D (b) (all pages); loses activity-scope information that some index variants might want.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-25 (D-D); `_NA_` added to the value set (enum change, two version steps); CX-11's QC check unchanged.

options.label: Agent-drafted: re-word to the publishing system
options.mechanism: Re-word the question: 'Is this page part of a disclosure channel that reports for one institution, several, or the whole government (e.g. a national register, a sector inventory)? If the page is a one-off document, code single_institution.'
options.benefits: Keeps all-pages coding while anchoring on the channel; default value for one-off pages is explicit.
options.risks: New wording, unpiloted; still asked on pages where the answer is a default.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-21..CX-24 and a re-pilot (the frozen pilot text changes).

options.label: Agent-drafted: treat single_institution as the no-evidence value
options.mechanism: Keep the wording; classify `single_institution` (with `unknown`) as a no-evidence value for R-041, so only `multi_institution` and `whole_of_government` need a quote.
options.benefits: Avoids mass downgrade for lack of a quote; no change to frozen text.
options.risks: Asymmetric treatment of values; `single_institution` published without support.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-041 value list (Q-010 a), PI approval; T-024 test.

items.name: evaluation_documented (CX-30..CX-40, incl. CX-32b/c/d, CX-33)
items.current_text:
Question to jev: *Does this page document an evaluation of this GenAI activity?* One value. If several fit, take the first in table order.

- `results_reported`: The page states that this activity was tested, evaluated, audited or monitored **and** reports a result (a metric, a finding or a conclusion).
- `conducted_no_results`: The page states that an evaluation, test, audit, pilot review or monitoring took place or is in place, but reports no result.
- `required_or_planned`: The page states that an evaluation is required (by a rule) or planned, with no evidence that it has happened. A policy finding that requires evaluation of GenAI tools takes this value.
- CX-32b: A requirement to carry out a risk or impact assessment is **not** `required_or_planned`; it belongs to `has_risk_assessment` alone (consistent with CX-37).
- CX-32c: A clause requiring periodic review of the GenAI policy itself counts as `required_or_planned`. This includes any policy with a GenAI section (e.g. a general IT policy).
- CX-32d: A required pre-use review that mixes fitness-for-purpose with security or compliance checks counts as `required_or_planned`. A pure risk or impact assessment requirement stays under CX-32b.
- `unclear`: The page makes an evaluative statement, but its subject, or whether it concerns this GenAI activity, cannot be settled. An evaluation clearly of a different tool or activity is `not_documented`, not `unclear`.
- `not_documented`: The page has no evaluation statement about this activity.
- CX-35..CX-39: no negative value; outcome claims need a described evaluation; risk/impact assessment counts only with testing or measured performance; vendor claims need a named institutional or independent evaluator; a pilot stage alone is `not_documented`.

findings.evidence: Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: 26 of the 36 positive codes (results_reported 9/12, required_or_planned 10/17, conducted_no_results 7/7) and 47 of 249 not_documented
findings.text: Under R-081 (SPEC.md:133) 72% of the positive evaluation codes in pilot 2 would be downgraded, so the field would publish about 10 positives in 285 finding pages. The 47 low-confidence `not_documented` answers would go to 'unclear/unknown': `unknown` is not a value of this field and `unclear` has a specific signed meaning (CX-33, an evaluative statement whose subject is unsettled), so R-081 either needs a new value or overloads `unclear`.

CX-32c counts a clause requiring periodic review of the GenAI policy document (including a general IT policy with a GenAI section) as `required_or_planned` evaluation. Reviewing a policy text is not evaluating an AI system's performance; this makes most GenAI policies score on the governance 'evaluation' component, which then co-moves with `activity_type = policy_guidance` (itself an interim governance component, P-3 (c), INDEX-DECISIONS.md:13).

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:21 (CX-02: state = page text plus activity_name, activity_type, adoption_stage, tool_name); Stage5-Rulings.md:31 (DEC-010 a: jev sees page with span marked); SPEC.md:63 (R-004)
findings.text: The frozen instrument conditions on four finding fields. In v2.7, `activity_type` and `adoption_stage` are themselves pass-2 jev codes for the same activity and `activity_name`/`tool_name` are extractor free text. Either evaluation_documented runs in a second pass-2 round after those codes (cost, latency, error propagation), or the state differs from the signed one (span marker only), which means the question is byte-identical but the instrument is not.

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:184; pilot/pilot.py:236-238 (min over table order across chunks)
findings.text: Combination takes the first value in table order found in any chunk. The activity's span (DEC-010) lies in one chunk; in the other chunks 'this activity' is undefined, so an evaluative statement about anything else on a long page yields `unclear` or worse and beats `not_documented`. This inflates positives and `unclear` on long policy PDFs.

Agent read 25/5/10 on 40 pages (10 can't-tell), with remaining vendor-trial, missed-trial and CX-32b/32d boundary errors. C2-C4 wording (CX-32c scope, CX-32d, CX-33 different-tool rule) has never been run; R-084 replaces the gold set with a fixture test only.
Boilerplate such as 'usage will be monitored' or 'the service is monitored for quality' sits between CX-31 (in place) and CX-32 (planned) and is common in policies and terms-of-use pages.

options.label: Keep CX-30..CX-40 as signed
options.mechanism: Pass-2 jev Choice per (page x activity), first-in-order across chunks.
options.benefits: No re-signature; preserves the signed boundary choices (D-E..D-G, C2-C4).
options.risks: On pilot-2 confidences most positives are downgraded; the R-081 downgrade target for low-confidence `not_documented` is undefined; state differs from CX-02.
options.commits_to: R-025; a SPEC ruling on the R-081 target for this field (no CX change); explicit pass-2 ordering so CX-02's state exists.

options.label: Agent-drafted: narrow CX-32c to evaluation of AI systems
options.mechanism: Delete CX-32c's policy-review clause: a periodic review of the policy document is `not_documented` unless it requires testing, monitoring or evaluation of GenAI tools or their outputs.
options.benefits: Keeps 'evaluation' about system performance; reduces co-movement with policy_guidance.
options.risks: Reverses W3 = b and C3 = a (two signed rulings); policy-heavy institutions score lower.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-32c; fixture pages (R-084); no enum change.

options.label: Agent-drafted: add an explicit low-confidence value
options.mechanism: Add `unknown` to the value set as the R-081 target for any low-confidence answer, distinct from CX-33 `unclear`.
options.benefits: Keeps `unclear` meaning what CX-33 signed; R-081 becomes mechanically applicable.
options.risks: Enum change; index decision P-5 needs a rule for `unknown` in the governance score.
options.commits_to: Re-signature; two contract-version steps (C-007); procurement notified if it consumes the field.

options.label: Agent-drafted: two-step question
options.mechanism: Step 1 jev Choice: does the page contain an evaluation statement about the marked activity (yes/no/cannot tell)? Step 2, only if yes: the four-value kind (results / conducted / required-planned / unclear subject).
options.benefits: Each step is simpler and better suited to jev; the gate makes chunk combination cleaner (step 1 any-yes across chunks that contain the span).
options.risks: Departs from the piloted single question; two requests per activity.
options.commits_to: Re-signature and re-pilot; question-set version bump.

T-011 must stay byte-identical to the signed text unless re-signed (PLAN.md T-011).

items.name: evaluation_type_* (CX-41, six yes/no, gated)
items.current_text: Included. Asked only when `evaluation_documented` ∈ {`results_reported`, `conducted_no_results`, `required_or_planned`}; six yes/no items: `pre_deployment_testing`, `pilot_evaluation`, `independent_audit`, `ongoing_monitoring`, `user_feedback`, `bias_or_safety_testing`.

findings.evidence: SPEC.md:98, :133 (R-041, R-081); PLAN.md:1153 (T-024 downgrade after both passes)
findings.text: The gate reads `evaluation_documented`, which may later be downgraded (no quote, or confidence < 0.8: 26 of 36 positives in pilot 2, see X03). Nothing says whether type items asked under a since-downgraded gate are voided, kept, or re-asked. If kept, the pilot-1 defect (40 type yes without evaluation, PILOT-REPORT.md:25) returns by the back door.

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:85; pilot/pilot.py:217 (question: 'documents an evaluation, or a requirement or plan for one')
findings.text: Because `required_or_planned` opens the gate, a yes on `pre_deployment_testing` can mean 'testing was done' or 'testing is required'. The type items carry no done/required distinction, so they cannot be read as types of conducted evaluation.

findings.evidence: Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8 (of 36 gated pages): pre_deployment_testing 20, ongoing_monitoring 25, pilot_evaluation 14
findings.text: Most type answers for the two most common types fall below 0.8 (binary jev confidence is 2p-1, so 0.8 means p >= 0.9; verified on all 3,066 binary answers in the same file). After R-081, `ongoing_monitoring` and `pre_deployment_testing` would be mostly `unknown`, a value these yes/no items do not have.

Two items are near-constant. Categories overlap by design (a pilot evaluation that included bias testing is yes on both), which is fine for multi-select but should be stated; there is no `other` type.

options.label: Keep CX-41 as signed
options.mechanism: Second jev request when the combined gate value is positive; six binary Choices; any-yes across chunks.
options.risks: Gate/downgrade order undefined; required vs done mixed; no `unknown` for R-081.
options.commits_to: R-025; a T-024 rule that type items follow the final (post-downgrade) gate.

options.label: Agent-drafted: gate on the post-downgrade value
options.mechanism: Procedural: ask (or keep) type items only if `evaluation_documented` is still positive after R-041 and R-081; otherwise store `_NA_`.
options.benefits: Prevents types without a supported evaluation; no wording change.
options.risks: Adds a dependency between T-024 and pass 2 (may need a third jev round, or post-hoc voiding).
options.commits_to: No re-signature if wording unchanged (procedural, PI approval); `_NA_` handling in T-012 enums.

options.label: Agent-drafted: restrict gate to conducted evaluations
options.mechanism: Ask types only when `evaluation_documented` in {results_reported, conducted_no_results}.
options.benefits: Types then describe evaluations that happened.
options.risks: Loses type information for planned/required evaluations (17 of 36 gated pages in pilot 2).
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-41 (D-H).

options.label: Agent-drafted: drop the two near-constant items
options.mechanism: Remove `independent_audit` and `bias_or_safety_testing`, or merge them into one `external_or_safety_review` item.
options.risks: Loses rare but substantively important signals; Kaser comparability.
options.commits_to: Re-signature; schema change (version steps).

items.notes: **Frozen (CX-01.2, signed 2026-10-25; SPEC R-025, SPEC.md:78).** Any alternative below other than `keep` requires PI re-signature of the CX row, a re-pilot or at least the R-084 fixture test for the changed wording, and (for any enum change) two contract-version steps (C-007, SPEC.md:221). T-011 must stay byte-identical to the signed text unless re-signed (PLAN.md T-011).

items.name: content_* descriptive items (purpose, tool_or_model, vendor, data, users, status_date)
items.current_text: Items: `content_purpose` (what the tool is used for), `content_tool_or_model` (product or model named), `content_vendor` (supplier named), `content_data` (data inputs or data handled described), `content_users` (who uses it or who is affected), `content_status_date` (deployment status or date stated) ... each `yes` / `no` (yes = stated on the page).

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:20 (CX-01: page fields); pilot/pilot.py:203 ('Does the page state this about the GenAI activity'), :220-225 (state includes one `genai_activity`)
findings.text: CX-01 defines `content_*` as page fields coded in pass 1, but the frozen pilot asked them about one named GenAI activity, with that finding in the state. In v2.7 pass 1 runs before segmentation (R-002/R-003, SPEC.md:61-62), so no activity exists yet. Asking 'about the GenAI activity' with none in the state is a different instrument from the one piloted; on a two-activity page it is undefined which activity's vendor counts.

findings.evidence: pilot sample drawn only from finding pages (PILOT-REPORT.md:10); PLAN.md:926 (T-022: quotes for positive CX page fields on every page, e.g. a `background_only` page)
findings.text: All pilot pages were confirmed-activity pages. v2.7 codes page fields on every page including `background_only`, `other_body` and `no_genai`. `content_vendor = yes` on a national-strategy page (background) or another body's page credits disclosure content to the institution unless the roll-up filters by verdict; there is no `_NA_` value for non-GenAI pages, and none of this was piloted.

findings.evidence: Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: status_date 124/285, data 99, users 84, vendor 82, tool_or_model 64, purpose 47
findings.text: Between 16% and 44% of answers fall below 0.8, about half of them `no`. R-081 sends low-confidence negatives to 'unknown', which these yes/no items do not have. P-7a ruled that `content_*` replace T2 (INDEX-DECISIONS.md:25), so the transparency index inherits this unknown share.

findings.evidence: PILOT-REPORT.md:24 (purpose 269, users 258 of 285 yes in pilot 1)
findings.text: `content_purpose` and `content_users` are near-constant on finding pages: almost any page that documents an activity says what it is for. They add little variance to the index; `content_status_date` mixes status and any date, so a publication date alone may satisfy it.

Any-yes across chunks raises yes rates mechanically with page length (8 of 285 pilot pages were chunked, 2-4 chunks each, agent count from answers-v2.jsonl.gz), so long documents score as more transparent partly because they are long.

options.label: Keep CX-50/51 descriptive items as signed
options.mechanism: Pass-1 binary Choices on every page; any-yes across chunks.
options.risks: Unpiloted grain (no activity in pass 1) and page coverage; R-081 target missing.
options.commits_to: R-025; a ruling on how the question refers to 'the GenAI activity' without an activity in state.

options.label: Agent-drafted: move content_* to pass 2 (per page x activity)
options.mechanism: Ask the six items per activity with the span marked, like the pilot did; page value = any-yes over activities if a page value is needed.
options.benefits: Matches the piloted instrument; attributes content to an activity; naturally skips non-activity pages.
options.risks: Contradicts CX-01's 'page field' grain (signed); more jev questions per page.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-01 for these items; T-011/T-021/T-023 scope change; no enum change.

options.label: Agent-drafted: keep page grain, gate by verdict
options.mechanism: Ask `content_*` only on pages with a GenAI-bearing verdict (the five R-003 values); store `_NA_` otherwise; reword to 'about any GenAI activity on the page'.
options.benefits: Avoids crediting background or no-GenAI pages; defines the referent.
options.risks: New wording, unpiloted; `_NA_` is a new value.
options.commits_to: Re-signature; enum change (two version steps); re-pilot.

options.label: Agent-drafted: drop near-constant items from the index
options.mechanism: Keep all items in the codebook but mark `content_purpose` and `content_users` as descriptive-only (not index components).
options.benefits: Index variance comes from discriminating items; no coding change.

items.name: CX coding grain and jev state (CX-01, CX-02, CX-05)
items.current_text:
- CX-01: **Page fields** (`disclosure_form`, `disclosure_scope`, the optional `content_*` items) are properties of the source page. They are coded once per (institution × page), on the stored page text, and copied to every evidence row from that page.
- CX-02: **Finding fields** (`evaluation_documented`, optional `evaluation_type_*`) are coded per (finding × page). The state given to jev is the page text plus that finding's `activity_name`, `activity_type`, `adoption_stage` and `tool_name`.
- CX-05: The raw jev answer is stored with its probability distribution, confidence, response model id and request id.

findings.evidence: codebook-extension-proposal.md:204 ('Frozen instrument: this file at CX-01.2 plus the question text in pilot/pilot.py (v2) and pilot/contact.py'); pilot/pilot.py:220-225; Stage5-Rulings.md:31
findings.text: R-025 and T-011 protect question text byte-for-byte, but jev answers depend on the state too. The pilot state carried institution, country, one finding (4 fields), URL, page title, 'page_part i of n' and a character-chunked page. v2.7 pass 1 has no finding; pass 2 has a span marker; chunks are token-based (DEC-008 c, Stage5-Rulings.md:29). Byte-identical questions over a different state are not the signed instrument, and pilot agreement figures do not transfer automatically.

A page shared by several institutions (a regional register, a ministry page listing agencies) is coded once per institution, so the same page can receive different `disclosure_form` codes for different institutions. Followed pages (R-031) add more shared pages.

items.name: Supporting text per code (R-040)
items.current_text: For every jev code on a page or activity, the extractor (C-001) extracts the verbatim supporting text from the page, after jev has coded.

findings.text: The extractor is told the code and asked for support. A capable model will almost always find some verbatim sentence near the topic, and R-042 checks only that the sentence exists in the page. A wrong code with an on-topic quote passes. G-002 ('every published classification code is backed by verbatim supporting text', SPEC.md:25) is then true of presence, not of support; the downgrade rule mainly catches fabricated quotes and genre/absence codes with no natural quote (X01, X02).

R-040 says 'every jev code'; R-041 and Q-010 a say only positive or substantive codes need support. T-022 follows Q-010 a (PLAN.md:926). R-040's wording should match, or the extractor is asked for quotes for `no` codes it cannot support.

findings.evidence: extract output_contract.md:127 (old `source_snippet`: English translation with original in parentheses)
findings.text: Verbatim quotes on ja/zh/other pages (two-thirds of pilot strata, PILOT-REPORT.md:10) are unreadable for most users and the PI audit; v2.7 has no translation field. See X41.
The extractor prompt must allow 'no support found' explicitly; otherwise its incentive is to return something.

items.name: Quote presence check (R-042)
items.current_text: Supporting text is checked against the stored page text by fuzzy match; a quote below the match threshold counts as no supporting text.

findings.text: Partial-ratio fuzzy matching of a short quote ('AI', 'ChatGPT', a city name, one CJK term) matches almost any relevant page. No minimum quote length or minimum distinctiveness is set; CJK quotes are short in characters by nature.

findings.evidence: SPEC.md:100 (R-044 'quote from the chunk that produced the code'); PLAN.md:1153
findings.text: Matching against the whole page lets a quote from chunk 3 support a chunk-1 code; matching against the producing chunk loses evidence that straddles a chunk boundary (no overlap rule in DEC-008).
Hyphenation, ligatures and line breaks in PDF text make verbatim quotes differ from stored text; the threshold must be calibrated per content type, which T-003 may not cover.

options.risks: Short quotes pass trivially.
options.commits_to: T-003 spike and PI threshold approval.

options.mechanism: Require a minimum quote length (in characters, script-adjusted) and match against the producing chunk plus a fixed overlap window.
options.risks: Some legitimate short evidence (a table cell) fails.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-042 (PI); T-020 overlap; T-024 tests.

options.mechanism: The extractor returns character offsets into the chunk (as DEC-010 does for spans); the quote is cut deterministically from stored text.
options.benefits: Quotes are verbatim by construction; fuzzy matching only validates offsets.
options.risks: Offsets from an LLM can be off; needs a repair rule.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta; T-022/T-032/T-024 changes.

items.name: Downgrade rule (R-041)
items.current_text: A positive or substantive code with no supporting text is downgraded: field to `unknown` (or the field's no-evidence value); institution verdict to `unclear` when no supported positive remains. Only positive or substantive values need support; `no`, `unknown`, `not_documented`, `_NA_` and negative page verdicts need none.

findings.text: R-041 names targets for fields and the institution verdict, but not for a page verdict. An unsupported `confirms_activity` page has no `unknown` verdict to fall to; `ambiguous_genai` and `ambiguous_attribution` assert specific doubts the page may not have. The pass-2 activity codes on that page then have an undefined status.

findings.type: no-evidence values per field not listed
findings.evidence: SPEC.md:98; PLAN.md T-024 spec-change trigger 'a field has no defined no-evidence value'
findings.text: For yes/no items (`content_*`, `evaluation_type_*`) the no-evidence value is `no`, so an unsupported yes becomes an asserted `no` published as a finding rather than a missing value. For `evaluation_documented` it becomes `not_documented`; for `disclosure_scope`, is `single_institution` substantive? Each field needs an explicit target in the codebook.

Downgrades cascade: page verdict -> pass-2 activity codes -> gated type items -> Stage 6 verdict. The order of application and whether dependent codes are voided or re-asked is not specified (see X04).

Downgrades fall where quotes are hard (genre, scope, absence-like values, non-Latin scripts if matching is weaker). With P-5 (b), downgraded pages leave the index denominator, so missingness is not at random.

options.mechanism: T-024 downgrades unsupported positive codes to `unknown` or the field's no-evidence value.
options.risks: Undefined page-verdict target; yes/no items turn into asserted `no`.
options.commits_to: Per-field targets still to be written in T-010.

options.mechanism: Add a codebook column `downgrade_to` for every item (e.g. page verdict `confirms_activity` -> `ambiguous_genai`; yes/no items -> `unknown`, adding the value; genre -> `unknown`).
options.benefits: Makes R-041 executable and auditable; programmatic linkage can read the column.
options.risks: Adds `unknown` to yes/no items (enum change; CX items need re-signature).
options.commits_to: Codebook column; CX re-signature where values are added; two version steps.

options.mechanism: Do not rewrite the value; publish the jev value plus `support_status` (supported / no_quote / low_confidence) and let consumers filter (X40).
options.benefits: No information loss; no new enum values in the CX fields.
options.risks: Reverses S8 a's 'not published as positive'; website must hide unsupported values.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to G-002/R-041 (PI ruling); D-007 interface.

items.name: Confidence threshold 0.8 for all jev codes (R-081)
items.current_text: One confidence threshold for all jev codes: 0.8. A code below 0.8 is downgraded as under R-041. This includes negative and absence codes: a page or field coded negative below 0.8 goes to `unclear` / `unknown`.

findings.type: scale of downgrade on CX fields
findings.evidence: Agent-computed from `pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz` (pilot 2, n = 285 finding pages, jev-1.13.0), not a reported pilot statistic: share of answers with jev confidence < 0.8: disclosure_scope 48%, content_status_date 44%, content_contact (pilot-2 wording) 43%, content_data 35%, evaluation_documented 26% (72% of its positives); report-v2.json confidence_quartiles
findings.text: Applied to the CX fields as piloted, the threshold turns several items into mostly-unknown fields. This was not visible when the threshold was ruled; no pilot report applied it.

findings.evidence: Agent check on pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz: for all 3,066 binary answers confidence = 2p - 1 exactly; PILOT-REPORT.md:95 (precision 61% at confidence >= 0.8 for confirms_activity)
findings.text: For yes/no items 0.8 means p >= 0.9; for multi-value items the mapping differs (e.g. p = 0.89 gave confidence 0.85 on a 4-value item). One threshold therefore imposes different stringency by item cardinality, and pilot 4 shows 0.8 is not calibrated accuracy (61% agent-judged precision above it).
`content_*`, `evaluation_type_*` and `evaluation_documented` have no `unknown`; R-081's target for their low-confidence negatives does not exist without an enum change to frozen items.

Undefined: whether the threshold applies per chunk before combination or to the combined code (and which confidence a combined code carries), and how it applies to derived codes (`content_contact` OR).

options.label: Keep one threshold 0.8 for all codes
options.mechanism: T-024 downgrades every jev answer below 0.8.
options.risks: Mass `unknown` on several CX items; undefined targets.
options.commits_to: Enum additions to CX items or a per-field target rule (X14).

options.label: Agent-drafted: probability threshold by cardinality
options.mechanism: Threshold on the chosen value's probability (e.g. p >= 0.8 for every item), not jev's confidence.
options.benefits: Same meaning across binary and multi-value items.
options.risks: Different numbers from the ruled 0.8; needs re-sizing.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-081 (PI ruling); T-024; quality packet re-sized.

options.label: Agent-drafted: per-item thresholds from fixtures
options.mechanism: Set thresholds per item at Stage 3 from the R-084 fixtures and the agent read (as Q-020 b does for the matcher).
options.benefits: Calibrated to observed error; avoids gutting low-confidence-but-accurate items.

items.name: Chunk combination rule (R-044, CX §11.1)
items.current_text: Chunked pages (> 32k tokens, C-004): the CX-01.2 §11.1 combination rule applies to every field. Page fields take the first chunk's value; yes/no items are yes if any chunk says yes; ordered vocabularies take the first value in table order found in any chunk. The supporting quote comes from the chunk that produced the code.

findings.type: page verdict and completeness swept in
findings.evidence: SPEC.md:100 ('applies to every field'), :61 (R-002: verdict and completeness are page-level codes); codebook-extension-proposal.md:184 (§11.1 names only disclosure_form and disclosure_scope as first-chunk fields)
findings.text: Read literally, R-044 makes the page verdict and page completeness 'page fields' that take the first chunk's value. A long council-minutes PDF whose GenAI item is in chunk 3 would get `no_genai`; a page whose 'see full report' link is in chunk 2 would be 'complete'. §11.1 itself limited first-chunk to the two CX page fields. The verdict needs its own rule (e.g. an order over the 8 values), which belongs to the page-verdict reviewer but is triggered by this wording.
`content_*` are both 'page fields' (CX-01) and 'yes/no items'; R-044 lists the two rules without precedence. §11.1 resolves it (any-yes), R-044 does not.

Pass-2 codes on chunked pages: the activity span lies in one chunk; the other chunks contain no marked activity. Running pass 2 on all chunks with an order rule inflates evaluation codes (X03); running it only on the span's chunk loses evidence elsewhere on the page.

findings.evidence: pilot/pilot.py:229-238 (combined answer = the first yes chunk's answer object)
findings.text: The pilot kept the first yes chunk's confidence. With R-081, taking the first, max or min confidence changes outcomes; not specified.

options.label: Keep R-044 as approved
options.mechanism: As written.
options.risks: Literal reading breaks page verdict and completeness.
options.commits_to: T-020/T-022 implementation; A-021 fixtures.

options.label: Agent-drafted: name the fields per rule
options.mechanism: Replace 'page fields' with an explicit list: first chunk = `disclosure_form`, `disclosure_scope`; any-yes = `content_*`, completeness 'incomplete', `evaluation_type_*`; ordered = `evaluation_documented`, page verdict (order to be ruled); state that combined confidence is the producing chunk's.

options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-044 (PI); codebook column; A-021 fixtures updated.

options.label: Agent-drafted: pass 2 on the span's chunk plus neighbours
options.mechanism: Pass-2 questions run on the chunk containing the span and its adjacent chunks only.
options.risks: Misses evidence elsewhere in long documents.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta; T-023.

items.name: Page completeness (R-030)
items.current_text: The first pass also records whether the page holds all available information about every activity it mentions, or links to further pages with information about any of them.

findings.text: 'All available information' requires knowledge of what exists elsewhere; jev sees only the page. The answerable question is narrower: does the page point to another document or page for more information about a GenAI activity it mentions (e.g. 'read the full report', 'see the policy', an attachment)? As worded, every short press release is plausibly 'incomplete'.

findings.type: links are not in stored text
findings.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/scrape/render.py:65-82 (RenderedPage: url, text, title, content_type, fetch_metadata; no links); html.py:36-67 (extract_links exists but is not persisted)
findings.text: jev can say 'incomplete' because the text says 'see attached report', but the stored text carries no hrefs, so the extractor cannot return a URL unless one is printed in the text. In the back-fill (R-035, stored pages) most follow-up links would be unrecoverable without re-fetching the page.

findings.evidence: SPEC.md:85; PLAN.md:927 (links for every incomplete page whatever its verdict)
findings.text: On `no_genai` pages completeness is vacuous; on `background_only` and `other_body` pages following links pulls in other bodies' pages. No gating by verdict is defined.

options.mechanism: jev binary in pass 1; extractor returns links for incomplete pages.
options.risks: Unanswerable construct; links missing from stored text.
options.commits_to: T-011 wording; T-022 links.

options.label: Agent-drafted: 'refers onward' question
options.mechanism: jev Choice: 'Does the page refer the reader to another page or document for more information about a GenAI activity it mentions?' yes / no; asked only on the five R-003 verdicts.
options.benefits: Answerable from text; fewer wasted fetches.
options.risks: Misses incompleteness the page does not signal.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-030 (PI); T-011.

options.label: Agent-drafted: deterministic link candidates plus jev selection
options.mechanism: Persist `extract_links` output (X42); jev picks, per candidate link (anchor text + context), whether it leads to more information about the activity.
options.benefits: Uses real hrefs; selection is a jev classification (R-001), not extractor judgement.
options.risks: Many questions per link-heavy page; scrape change.
options.commits_to: Scrape-layer change (PI ruling vs N-004); T-011/T-025; cost estimate.

items.name: Follow-up links (R-031..R-036)
items.current_text: R-031: When a page is not complete, the LLM extracts the follow-up links and they are sent back to the scrape phase; fetched pages then pass through the same classification. R-032: ... up to 3 hops ... A per-institution cap on followed URLs also applies ... R-033: Any link the page cites is eligible, including news and vendor pages. R-034: Each URL is fetched at most once per institution per run; every followed link records the page it came from (provenance chain). R-036: Pages fetched live during the back-fill are new source records tagged with their provenance ... They count as evidence but sit outside the original searched sample and never add to its denominator.

findings.text: In ordinary v2.7 runs, followed pages enlarge each institution's page set (up to 3 hops), which raises the chance of a `yes` relative to v2.5 runs. R-036's 'outside the searched sample' rule applies only to the back-fill. Prevalence across v2.5 and v2.7 rows (both visible on the site, R-051) is then not comparable without a per-source `discovery_path` (searched vs followed).

findings.evidence: PILOT-REPORT.md:98 (main pilot-4 error: parent or neighbouring body's activity credited to a smaller unit)
findings.text: Followed links from a village or ward page often lead to the district or county; R-033 allows any link. This feeds the error mode the unclear pilot found most often, unless followed pages are coded with `other_body` correctly.
Choosing which of a page's links are 'follow-up' links is a relevance classification done by the extractor. That sits uneasily with R-001 (codes by jev only).
See X17: hrefs are not persisted, so the extractor sees only URLs printed in text.

options.label: Keep R-031..R-036
options.mechanism: Extractor returns links; follow leg up to 3 hops and a URL cap; provenance stored.
options.risks: Comparability and attribution risks; missing hrefs.
options.commits_to: T-025; PI sets the cap after T-002.

options.label: Agent-drafted: tag discovery path on every source
options.mechanism: Add a deterministic `discovery_path` (searched / followed hop n / back-fill followed) on every source row in all runs, and report prevalence with and without followed pages.
options.risks: One more column.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta extending R-036 to all runs; D-007 field.

options.label: Agent-drafted: restrict eligible links
options.mechanism: Follow only links on the same registrable domain as the page or the institution's official domain (X37), plus document attachments.
options.risks: Misses news/vendor detail (reverses Q6b ii).
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-033 (PI ruling).

items.name: Supporting-text publication and length (R-043, DEC-016)
items.current_text: Supporting text is published with the code it supports. The API carries the full text; the website shows it up to a display cap, with a marker and access to the full text. (DEC-016 c: cap on website only, full text in API; cap value proposed by agent after T-003, PI sets.)

findings.text: There is no cap on quote length at extraction or in the API. Long verbatim passages from news and vendor pages (third_party was 43% of the pilot, PILOT-REPORT.md:21) published in a bulk API raise reuse issues; quotes for contact items contain officials' names (X06).
One quote per code per page, many codes per page: the API payload per activity grows with every new field; no de-duplication of identical quotes across codes.

options.mechanism: Full text in API; website cap set after T-003.
options.risks: Unbounded API text.
options.commits_to: T-003 cap proposal; D-007.

options.mechanism: The extractor returns at most N characters (script-adjusted) per quote; the same cap applies in API and site.
options.risks: Some codes need longer context.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-043; T-022/T-032 prompts.

options.label: Agent-drafted: offsets for third-party sources
options.mechanism: For third-party sources publish offsets, length and a hash plus the URL; full text only internally.
options.risks: Users cannot read the support without visiting the page.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta (PI); D-007.

items.name: Contract version per row (R-050)
items.current_text: Every published row carries the contract version that produced it.

findings.evidence: SPEC.md:107; Stage5-Rulings.md:26 (DEC-005 a), :25 (DEC-004 a: model id per jev answer); C-001 (SPEC.md:215, extractor model changed by delta)
findings.text: A v2.7 row is produced by the jev question-set version, jev model version, the extractor model and prompt hash (already changed once by RC-D-001), the chunker estimator, the matcher threshold (T-003) and the confidence threshold. 'Contract version' alone does not identify these; a change of extractor model or matcher threshold within v2.7 would be invisible on the row.

Scenarios still say v2.6 for rows this plan labels v2.7 (DEC-013 a).

items.name: source_type (Group E col 33, §4.6)
items.current_text:
| `official_gov` | Government domain (.gov, .gouv, .go, etc.), gazette, parliamentary record |
| `procurement_tender` | Tender notice, RFP, contract award, vendor selection document |
| `news_major` | Major national/international news outlet (Reuters, BBC, NYT, Le Monde, NHK, etc.) |
| `news_trade` | Technology or government trade press (GovTech, FedScoop, PublicTechnology, etc.) |
| `vendor` | Vendor website, case study, blog post, or press release |
| `academic` | Peer-reviewed paper, working paper, university report |
| `policy_org` | Think tank, IGO, or policy organization (OECD, World Bank, ITU, Brookings, etc.) |
| `social_media` | Official social media accounts (Twitter/X, LinkedIn from institutional accounts) |
| `archive` | Wayback Machine, Google Cache, or other archived page |
| `other` | None of the above; explain in `source_snippet` |

findings.evidence: PLAN.md:866 (T-021 pass-1 artifact: verdict, CX page fields, completeness, chunk ids), :925-929 (T-022 extractor scope), SPEC.md:60 (R-001), :64 (R-006)
findings.text: In v2.5 the extractor (nano) coded `source_type`. In v2.7 the extractor may not classify (R-001, C-001), and no T-0xx card asks jev for it or derives it. Yet it is a published column (validate contract §5.1 col 7, output_contract.md:127), feeds `source_credibility` (X22), the Stage 6 tie-break (X31), the CX QC cross-check (codebook-extension-proposal.md:45) and the pilot strata.

Categories mix publisher (government, vendor, news), document kind (tender, academic paper), channel (social media) and access path (archive). A tender on a government portal, a vendor press release on a news wire, an institution's own LinkedIn post, a Wayback copy of a ministry page all fit two values; there is no order rule.

'Government domain (.gov, .gouv, .go, etc.)' misses many official sites (.org, .lg.jp, .de municipal sites, .ac for public universities) and includes government-hosted third-party content. The project already holds an official-site overlay (master-sites, commit c6349d6) that could decide this deterministically.
`other` says 'explain in source_snippet'; v2.7 has no free-text home for that explanation.

options.commits_to: A card or ruling naming the coder before T-011.

options.mechanism: Add `source_type` to the pass-1 page question set with an order rule (first in table order) and the master official-site list in the state.

options.label: Agent-drafted: deterministic publisher + jev genre
options.mechanism: Deterministic `publisher_kind` from URL vs the master official-site overlay and known news/vendor lists; jev only for genre values (tender, academic, policy_org). Pair with X01 alt-2.
options.benefits: Reproducible; removes a classification from the LLM for the easy half.

options.mechanism: Drop `source_type` from v2.7 rows; publish `disclosure_form` (and its publisher dimension) instead; keep v2.5 values on v2.5 rows.

items.name: source_credibility hierarchy (col 35, §4.8)
items.current_text:
When sources conflict on coded values, the higher-credibility source wins:

1. **`high`**: Government domains, procurement/tender portals, parliamentary/council records, annual reports, regulator publications, gazette notices.
2. **`medium`**: Major news outlets, vendor case studies with named institutions, trade press, policy organization reports.
3. **`low`**: Social media, blog posts, undated pages, anonymous sources, machine-translated content you could not fully verify.

findings.text: Same gap as X21: no card produces `source_credibility`, but Stage 6 conflict resolution (validate output_contract.md:99-101; jev_validate.py:172-182) depends on it.
'Machine-translated content you could not fully verify' describes the old LLM coder's ability, not the source. It has no meaning for jev or a deterministic rule.
Tiers are a near-deterministic mapping of `source_type` plus 'undated'. Coding it separately adds a second, inconsistent judgement.

findings.type: construct: credibility vs recency for time-varying fields
findings.evidence: validate output_contract.md:101 (credibility first, then most recent date)
findings.text: For `adoption_stage` and `year_*`, an old official pilot announcement outranks a newer news report of production, so the consolidated stage can be stale. Credibility is a reasonable rule for identity facts, less so for status.

options.mechanism: As v2.5 text.
options.risks: No coder; coder-relative clause.
options.commits_to: A coder decision in T-010/T-011.

options.mechanism: `source_credibility` = fixed map from `source_type` (X21) plus `low` when `source_publication_date` = unknown; drop the translation clause.
options.risks: Loses case-level judgement (e.g. an anonymous news blog on a major outlet's domain).
options.commits_to: Codebook mapping table; T-024 or T-028; Stage 6 tests.

options.mechanism: Do not publish credibility; Stage 6 computes tiers internally from `source_type` when it needs a tie-break.
options.benefits: Removes a published judgement that users may over-read.

| `high` | Coded values are based on a primary government source or multiple corroborating secondary sources. |
| `medium` | Based on a single reputable secondary source without primary confirmation, OR primary source is ambiguous. |
| `low` | Based on indirect evidence, machine-translated sources with potential misinterpretation, or a single non-authoritative source. |

'Multiple corroborating secondary sources' is a cross-source property, but rows are per page (output_contract.md:41-43). The criterion can only be applied in Stage 6.
Stage 6 takes the maximum confidence across supporting rows: one high-confidence row hides several low ones.

items.name: uncertainty_flags vocabulary (col 39, §4.10)

items.name: Stage 6 institution verdict (R-005; validate v1.3 §3.1; v1.4 complete-context rule)
items.current_text:
R-005: ... institution-level `no` only with complete supplied context and no unresolved signal. An institution whose reviewed pages are all negative at confidence ≥ 0.8 gets `no` directly; the complete-context rule blocks `no` only when an unresolved signal remains (a low-confidence negative downgraded under R-081 counts as one).

v1.3 §3.1: `yes` <=> `len(activities) >= 1` AND >=1 source has `genai_evidence = confirms_activity`. `no` <=> `len(activities) == 0` AND every source has `genai_evidence = confirms_absence`. `unclear` <=> `len(activities) == 0` AND no source has `genai_evidence = confirms_activity` (sources are some mix of `ambiguous` / `background_only`; at least one such source exists).

findings.evidence: evidence_review.py@052fcb2:61-64, :111 (`inaccessible` disposition -> ambiguous); SPEC.md:71 (8 verdicts, no inaccessible); SPEC.md:65 ('reviewed pages')
findings.text: v2.6 kept inaccessible sources as unresolved signals. The v2.7 page vocabulary has no such value, and R-005 counts only 'reviewed pages'. An institution with one readable `no_genai` page and four failed fetches would get `no`. v1.4's pipeline coverage check (evidence_review.py@052fcb2:332-336: completion markers, attrition ledger, no non-benign failures) is not carried into R-005's wording.

findings.evidence: SPEC.md:65, :98 ('negative page verdicts'); validate output_contract.md diff v1.4 §9 last paragraph (benign background_only allowed alongside an excluded event)
findings.text: Which of `no_genai`, `confirms_absence`, `event_only`, `other_body`, `background_only` count as negative for `no` is not stated. Under v1.3 any `background_only` page forces `unclear` (validate output_contract.md:58), so an institution with four no-GenAI pages and one national-strategy page stays unclear; v1.4 relaxed this only for the event case. The choice moves many institutions between `no` and `unclear`.
Whether an incomplete page whose links were not followed (cap reached, fetch failed) is an unresolved signal is not stated.

cross_cutting.text: **Source-level fields have no coder in v2.7.** `source_type`, `source_credibility`, row `confidence`, `uncertainty_flags`, `source_publication_date`, `source_language`, `source_snippet`, `source_title` and `institution_summary` were all written by the old extractor. R-001/C-001 bar the new extractor from classifying, and no T-0xx card asks jev for them or derives them; the pass-1 artifact is verdict + CX page fields + completeness + chunk ids. Stage 6 tie-breaks, index decision P-6 and the CX QC cross-check all depend on them. Items X21-X28, X33.
cross_cutting.evidence: PLAN.md:866 (T-021 output); PLAN.md:925-929 (T-022 scope); Stage5-Rulings.md:30 (DEC-009 a routing table); SPEC.md:60, :215; validate output_contract.md:99-101, :119-131; INDEX-DECISIONS.md:26

cross_cutting.text: **R-081 (one 0.8 threshold, negatives downgraded too) collides with the frozen CX vocabularies.** On pilot-2 answers it downgrades 48% of `disclosure_scope`, 26-44% of several `content_*` items and 72% of positive `evaluation_documented` codes; and the yes/no items and `evaluation_documented` have no `unknown` to fall to. Resolving it needs either an enum change to frozen items (re-signature + two version steps) or a SPEC ruling on per-field targets. jev confidence is 2p-1 on binary items, so 0.8 means p >= 0.9 there.
cross_cutting.evidence: SPEC.md:133; agent computation on pilot/answers-v2.jsonl.gz (n = 285, jev-1.13.0); report-v2.json confidence_quartiles; PILOT-REPORT.md:95

cross_cutting.text: **The frozen CX instrument includes a state that v2.7 changes.** The pilot asked page fields 'about the GenAI activity' with one finding in the state, on finding pages only, with character chunks. v2.7 asks page fields in pass 1 before any activity exists, on every page verdict, with token chunks; pass 2 uses a span marker instead of CX-02's four finding fields. Byte-identical question text (R-025, T-011) does not preserve the signed instrument, so pilot agreement figures do not carry over without at least the R-084 fixture test on the v2.7 state.

**Supporting text is presence-checked, not support-checked, and the extractor is told the code first.** G-002's guarantee is weaker than its wording; the downgrade rule mostly removes codes that have no natural quote (genre, scope, absence-like values), which is differential missingness that P-5 (b) then pushes out of the index denominator. Items X12-X14, X35.

**The scraper removes the evidence two items depend on.** Stored text strips `<footer>`, `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<aside>` and keeps no hrefs or mailto links. `content_contact_details` explicitly counts footers, CX-53 e-mail extraction needs mailto/footers, and R-030/R-031 follow-up links need hrefs; for the back-fill on stored pages these are largely unrecoverable.

**R-044 'applies to every field' would put the page verdict and completeness under the first-chunk rule.** §11.1 named only the two CX page fields. The page verdict needs its own combination order (other reviewer's item; flagged here because the rule text is in this scope).

**Pass-2 codes on non-confirming pages and downgrade cascades lack an order of operations** (page verdict -> activity codes -> CX-41 gate -> Stage 6). Without it, type items can survive a downgraded gate and Stage 6 can count activities from pages that cannot support `yes`.

**Privacy and reuse of published text are not addressed anywhere in the codebook.** Full verbatim quotes in the API (DEC-016 c), officials' names as contact quotes, and personal e-mail addresses (CX-53) go to a public API and a bulk third-party handoff.

**Label and wording drift in SPEC.** SC-01 and SC-07 still say v2.6 rows; R-006's notes and DEC-009/DEC-010 say 'nano' (PLAN.md:9 states nano means the extractor); R-040 says 'every jev code' while Q-010 a limits support to positive codes.

**Evidence limits.** Every pilot agreement figure cited here is against one model's read of 6,000-character excerpts on 40 pages (not a gold set, C-015/Q-024); R-084 replaced the gold set with fixtures. Confidence shares above are agent computations on stored pilot answers, not figures the pilot report published.
